items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Amanda Randolph was a very capable pianist and although I did not know music, I knew when it was well played and Amanda was the first woman I ever heard that played like a man.

ctx.x: Every chance I had, which was quite often, I would go to a movie where I would stay to see the films 2 or 3 times. The movie houses were called Nickel-Odeons because five cents is also known as a nickel and it cost only 5 cents admission to see two or three comedy films and a feature film of 5 reels. There was an electric piano with a drum attachment in the Nickel-Odeons and most of the films were westerns better known as cowboy films.

Most of the Nickel Odeons were on 5th Street. In one theatre that was in the prominent negro district on 5th Street, they had a woman pianist named Amanda Randolph who played for the films, and there were also vaudeville shows [Theater Owners Booking Association] of a circuit called T.O.B.A.^ I learned that the show people said that T.O.B.A., which was an agency, was called "tough on black actors", and I supposed it must have been because of the conditions they had to suffer in going from place to place. Most of…

Drake, of Drake and Walker Show, was a small man who had one leg shorter than the other and he played cornet and had one of those long coach horns which had three valves like the cornet and the bell of the horn was about two or three feet long. I did not know anything about jazz or styles but Drake and his band sounded good to me and it was different from the way the parade bands played. Of course he did not have as many musicians as a brass band which is the name for a parade band. He came often to this theatre…
